correctness.rationale: The inspected primary proof gives two Picard exceptional values \(a,b\) and the exact Riccati equation \(f'=\kappa(f-a)(f-b)\). The two remaining partially shared values are attained, so Vieta forces \(cd=ab\). Conversely, for any four distinct nonzero values with \(ab=cd\), setting \(\kappa=(c+d-a-b)^{-1}\) and \(f=(a-bq)/(1-q)\), \(q=\eta e^{\kappa(a-b)z}\), gives exactly \(f'=\kappa(f-a)(f-b)\). The identity \(\kappa(y-a)(y-b)-y=\kappa(y-c)(y-d)\) proves completeness of the four finite partially shared values.

value.rationale: The fresh paper classifies functions conditional on already having four partially shared values. The accepted result solves the inverse realizability problem for the values themselves: an unordered four-point subset of \(\mathbb C^*\) occurs nontrivially exactly when it admits an equal-product pairing. The converse is explicit, the Riccati coefficient is reconstructed directly from the values, and the result distinguishes the two vacuous Picard-exceptional values from the two attained shared values. This is a natural structural classification rather than a numerical or notational corollary.
